blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus told this story to some folks who loved money and were proud of how religious they were.

verses.text: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:

verses.text: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,

verses.text: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Every day that rich man went in and out of his gate. Every day Lazarus lay there, hungry and sick. The only ones who came near him were the street dogs. The rich man never hit him. He just never saw him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, God sees. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "God sees"] God sees. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "God sees"] The rich man walked past him every day, but God saw Lazarus.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Notice who gets a name in this story. The rich man has none. The beggar is called Lazarus, which means God helps.

verses.text: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;

verses.text: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Now everything was turned upside down. The man who had everything was the one begging.

verses.text: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

segments.speaker: richman
segments.text: Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Even now, he talked about Lazarus like somebody who could be sent to wait on him.

verses.text: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

segments.speaker: abraham
segments.text: Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

verses.text: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

segments.speaker: abraham
segments.text: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then the rich man thought about his brothers, still living the way he had lived.

verses.text: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:

segments.speaker: richman
segments.text: I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:

verses.text: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

segments.speaker: richman
segments.text: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

verses.text: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

segments.speaker: abraham
segments.text: They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

verses.text: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.

segments.speaker: richman
segments.text: Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.

verses.text: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

segments.speaker: abraham
segments.text: If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Moses and the prophets. They already had the word. God's word had told them all along to care for the poor and the stranger at the gate. A miracle would not change a heart that would not hear that.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, this story is not a map of the life to come. It is a warning for the life we are living now. The rich man's problem was not his money. It was that a hungry man lay at his door every day and he never once opened it. So the story asks us plainly. Who is lying at our gate? And will we see them while there is still time?

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Luke 16:19-31; says it is not a map of the life to come; no one told she is bound anywhere; the sin named is neglect.

cultural.note: 'God sees' at the turn; the poor man has the name and the dignity.
